name: comp17_folded_edge_and_room~full_ground^centred
architectural_reason: A folded section that locks a long tall body to a low slab, and the fold itself makes the sheltered entry rather than an applied canopy - the idea lives in the section, which is what development can carry further into floors and a core. It is also the only high-ranked figure on this board that has been taken to the size at which that idea is actually tested: 53% of the permitted ground and 204% of the permitted floor area, where the rest of the field sits at 20-35% coverage and 50-116% area. All six jurors of this round named that same failure - schemes never pushed to the scale where they would have to reckon with the parcel - so developing this parent asks the open question instead of repeating a comfortable one. The unresolved limit is the fold's deep interior: at this depth the section must earn its daylight, and development has to show how, or the folded roof becomes decoration over a dark plan.
